title: Kaoru — Personal AI assistant with agent capabilities
description: Talk, keep context and delegate coding and desktop tasks with Kaoru, a personal AI assistant with tools, memory, voice and a Live2D presence.
badge: Open source · Personal assistant with agent capabilities
hero:
Your AI assistant
for code and desktop.
intro: Kaoru talks with you, remembers context and stays with you through text, voice and a Live2D presence. When it is time to act, it can work as an agent: inspecting your project, preparing a plan, using tools and checking results under the permissions you configure.
note: Press the microphone to start listening. No wake word or continuous ambient listening.
caption: Kaoru’s Live2D avatar. You can choose another model with the appropriate usage rights.
featuresIntro: Talk with Kaoru, ask it to remember what matters or delegate a multi-step task. It can help across your project and desktop; available capabilities depend on your provider, operating system and permissions.
features: Explore files, dependencies and LSP symbols to inform a plan. Read and edit code, run commands and use Git. The structural index is bounded; references and file contents still need confirmation through project tools.
In the smart workflow, a recognized mutation triggers configured verification. Compatible focused tests run before general checks; a skipped or failed result does not count as a passed test.
Objectives, steps and evidence can persist in SQLite so work can continue. If storage falls back to memory, that continuity does not survive application shutdown.
Local memory retrieves facts, preferences and episodes related to a conversation. You can ask Kaoru to forget memories. Retrieved context may be included in a request to your AI provider.
Vosk transcribes audio locally; Edge TTS generates speech through a Microsoft service. Pressing the microphone interrupts playback. The avatar supports configurable models and gestures.

Open applications and websites, inspect accessible controls and use enabled screen, pointer or keyboard capabilities. Linux and Windows support semantic controls; macOS does not yet have equivalent coverage.
GitHub, optional Google Workspace, MCP servers and plugins expand available tasks. Each connection has its own permissions, dependencies and potential data transfers.
Configured sensors provide system and project signals. Proactivity evaluates context and policies to suggest help; it does not grant the model additional execution permissions.
Configure a compatible provider or a local endpoint. Quality, cost, vision and tool availability depend on the selected model and service.
flowIntro: Ask for guidance, continue a conversation or delegate a concrete result. When Kaoru acts as an agent, you can follow the plan and tool activity in chat; authorization and verification are part of execution.
flow: Examine the workspace, find relevant paths and consult available symbols.
Break the objective into steps with observable completion criteria.
Rules allow, ask about or block actions according to their scope.
Use tools and retain their results as evidence of the work.
Run checks; a failure can trigger repair or leave work pending.
securityIntro: Configure permissions for your task and device. The application separates model proposals from the controls that authorize tools.
security: Allow, ask and deny rules automate specific operations, request confirmation or block them. Not every action displays a prompt: the active policy determines that.

Applications, browser, screen, pointer, keyboard, processes and camera have independent controls. The current camera tool checks status or opens the camera application; it does not take photos or record video.
Electron windows are isolated from direct Node access. Command isolation is a separate mechanism and depends on the system’s capabilities and configuration.
Kaoru captures a baseline for recognized changes. Recovery has limits: remote actions, arbitrary commands and external effects may not be reversible.
Web and integration results are treated as untrusted content in the flows that delimit them. These controls reduce the risk of malicious instructions; they do not guarantee immunity.
Memory and embeddings are stored locally. Prompts may leave the device for your chosen provider. The system keychain is used when available; configuration backups require care.

audienceTitle: Set up Kaoru for the way you work
audience: Start with conversation, one workspace and the permissions you need. Enable voice, memory or suggestions to suit your routine; you can change the Live2D model.
Declare repository rules, prepare dependencies and configure verification commands. Review diffs and results before integrating important changes.
Define what information may reach the provider, who manages credentials and which tools are allowed. The code license does not cover characters or replace your organization’s policies.

guideIntro: Configuration, tasks and review criteria for using Kaoru on your device or in a client project.
guideSections: To install from source, you need Git, Node.js ≥ 18 and npm ≥ 9. Native modules are rebuilt for Electron; your system may also need build tools. Check the installation reference if a dependency fails.

Choose your provider and model in Kaoru’s settings. Use an authorized key or a compatible endpoint. Review your provider’s data policy, quotas and costs; open-source software does not include API usage. A local model does not automatically disconnect TTS, browsing or integrations.

Select the project folder from the chat toolbar. Prepare its dependencies and rules: Kaoru can incorporate AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or .cursorrules. Avoid including files unrelated to the task. Project rules guide the work; execution permissions are resolved separately.

Try: “Analyze how this form is validated, identify the relevant files and propose tests; do not edit yet.” Then authorize a specific change with an observable result. Review the plan, activity and diff, and cancel generation when you need to stop the run.

Configure your project’s commands. In smart mode, verification after recognized mutations can run quality scripts and a fallback JavaScript syntax check. Automatic focused selection recognizes tests/run-all.sh; other runners need configuration. Impact searches are approximate and do not replace integration tests.

Voice requires Python and configured ASR/TTS components. The microphone opens through an explicit action; pressing it interrupts Kaoru’s speech. Opening a URL uses your default browser; tasks that inspect pages use managed Chromium with a separate profile. Linux uses AT-SPI2 and Windows uses UI Automation for accessibility; macOS coverage is partial.

Connect only authorized accounts. Choose the scopes you need in GitHub and Google, and revoke access you no longer use. Review MCP and plugin origins and permissions. Start with a test repository before using client data, and agree on what context may leave the device.

Memory and durable objectives require working local storage. Keep backups before important operations. A checkpoint does not automatically undo actions in external services. Read-only subagents can investigate in parallel; subagents that modify the workspace run serially.

Check functionality, diffs, tests and reported limitations. Document the provider, permissions and data handling for that installation. For commercial distribution, use an avatar you own or have appropriate rights to: March 7th assets are not covered by MIT. This website does not offer a contractual support commitment or SLA.
